questionText: Consider the rigid bar ABC supported by the pin-jointed links BD and CE and subjected to a load $P$ at the end $A$ , as shown in the figure. The axial rigidities of $B D$ and $C E$ are 22500 kN and 15000 kN , respectively. If CE elongates by 5 mm due to the load P , the magnitude of the downward deflection (in mm ) of the end $A$ would be _________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
explanationHtml:
Given:
Rigid bar ABC is supported by pin-jointed links BD and CE.
CE elongates by 5,mm5 , \text{mm}5,mm.
Axial rigidity of BD = 22500,kN22500 , \text{kN}22500,kN, CE = 15000,kN15000 , \text{kN}15000,kN.
Geometry:
AB = BC = 200,mm200 , \text{mm}200,mm
BD = 200,mm200 , \text{mm}200,mm, CE = 300,mm300 , \text{mm}300,mm

Step 1: Use geometry to compute rotation
Let the bar rotate clockwise by angle θ\thetaθ.
Then, vertical displacement at point C = θ×300\theta \times 300θ×300
This equals elongation in CE:
⇒θ=5300=160,rad\Rightarrow \theta = \frac{5}{300} = \frac{1}{60} , \text{rad}⇒θ=3005​=601​,rad

Step 2: Vertical displacement at point A
From geometry, A is at horizontal distance 200,mm200 , \text{mm}200,mm from B
So vertical deflection at A:
ΔA=θ×200=160×200=20060≈3.33,mm\Delta_A = \theta \times 200 = \frac{1}{60} \times 200 = \frac{200}{60} \approx 3.33 , \text{mm}ΔA​=θ×200=601​×200=60200​≈3.33,mm

This is if only CE is active. But both BD and CE are axial links with given stiffness.
Let:
ΔD=\Delta_D =ΔD​= elongation in BD
ΔE=5,mm\Delta_E = 5 , \text{mm}ΔE​=5,mm (given)
From similar triangles formed by rotation about point B:
ΔD200=5300⇒ΔD=200300×5=103≈3.33,mm\frac{\Delta_D}{200} = \frac{5}{300} \Rightarrow \Delta_D = \frac{200}{300} \times 5 = \frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33 , \text{mm}200ΔD​​=3005​⇒ΔD​=300200​×5=310​≈3.33,mm

Step 3: Use force balance using stiffness
Force in BD = k1ΔD=22500×103=75000,Nk_1 \Delta_D = 22500 \times \frac{10}{3} = 75000 , \text{N}k1​ΔD​=22500×310​=75000,N
Force in CE = k2ΔE=15000×5=75000,Nk_2 \Delta_E = 15000 \times 5 = 75000 , \text{N}k2​ΔE​=15000×5=75000,N
So both members carry same force, balance is maintained.

Step 4: Displacement of point A
θ=ΔD200=103×200=160,rad\theta = \frac{\Delta_D}{200} = \frac{10}{3 \times 200} = \frac{1}{60} , \text{rad}θ=200ΔD​​=3×20010​=601​,rad
Distance from rotation center (B) to point A = 200+200+200+250=850,mm200 + 200 + 200 + 250 = 850 , \text{mm}200+200+200+250=850,mm
Displacement of A = θ×850=160×850=14.17≈14,mm\theta \times 850 = \frac{1}{60} \times 850 = 14.17 \approx 14 , \text{mm}θ×850=601​×850=14.17≈14,mm

Final Answer:
14,mm\boxed{14 , \text{mm}}14,mm​

But both BD and CE are axial links with given stiffness. Let: $\Delta_D =$ elongation in BD $\Delta_E = 5 , \text{mm}$ (given) From similar triangles formed by rotation about point B: $\frac{\Delta_D}{200} = \frac{5}{300} \Rightarrow \Delta_D = \frac{200}{300} \times 5 = \frac{10}{3} \approx 3.33 , \text{mm}$ Step 3: Use force balance using stiffness Force in BD = $k_1 \Delta_D = 22500 \times \frac{10}{3} = 75000 , \text{N}$ Force in CE = $k_2 \Delta_E = 15000 \times 5 = 75000 , \text{N}$ So both members carry same force, balance is maintained.Step 4: Displacement of point A $\theta = \frac{\Delta_D}{200} = \frac{10}{3 \times 200} = \frac{1}{60} , \text{rad}$ Distance from rotation center (B) to point A = $200 + 200 + 200 + 250 = 850 , \text{mm}$ Displacement of A = $\theta \times 850 = \frac{1}{60} \times 850 = 14.17 \approx 14 , \text{mm}$ Final Answer: $\boxed{14 , \text{mm}}$

questionText: An aircraft approaches the threshold of a runway strip at a speed of 200 km/h. The pilot decelerates the aircraft at a rate of 1.697 m/ $s^{2}$ and takes 18 s to exit the runway strip. If the deceleration after exiting the runway is 1 m/ $s^{2}$ , then the distance (in m, up to one decimal place) of the gate position from the location of exit on the runway is ______
explanationHtml:
Speed of aircraft,
ui=200  km/hr=200×10003600=55.56  m/s\begin{aligned} u_{i} &=200\; \text{km/hr} \\ &=\frac{200\times 1000}{3600}=55.56\; \text{m/s} \end{aligned}ui​​=200km/hr=3600200×1000​=55.56m/s​
Deceleration of aircraft on the runway =1.697m/s2=1.697 m/s^{2}=1.697m/s2

After runway aircraft decelerate with 1m/s21 m/s^{2}1m/s2

explanationText: Speed of aircraft, $\begin{aligned} u_{i} &=200\; \text{km/hr} \\ &=\frac{200\times 1000}{3600}=55.56\; \text{m/s} \end{aligned}$ Deceleration of aircraft on the runway $=1.697 m/s^{2}$ Aircraft takes 18 sec to exit the runway strip.Speed of the aircraft at the exit of the runway $\begin{aligned} u_{f} &=u_{i}+at \\ &=55.56-1.697\times 18 \\ &=25.014\; \text{m/s} \end{aligned}$ After runway aircraft decelerate with $1 m/s^{2}$ Total distance travelled by the aircraft from the location of exit on the runway $\begin{aligned} U^{2} &=u^{2}+2aS \\ 0 &=25.014^{2}-2\times 1\times S \\ S &=312.8\; \text{m} \end{aligned}$

explanationHtml:
Resultant force in x-direction,
Rx=Pcos⁡60∘−Qsin⁡15∘−Rsin⁡15∘=100cos⁡60∘−250sin⁡15∘−150sin⁡15∘=−159.59 kN(→)=−159.59 kN(→)=159.59 kN(←)\begin{aligned} R_{x}&=P\cos 60^{\circ}-Q\sin 15^{\circ}-R\sin 15^{\circ} \\ &=100\cos 60^{\circ}-250\sin 15^{\circ}-150\sin 15^{\circ} \\ &=-159.59\, kN\left ( \rightarrow \right ) \\ &=-159.59\, kN\left ( \rightarrow \right ) \\ &=159.59\, kN\left ( \leftarrow \right ) \end{aligned}Rx​​=Pcos60∘−Qsin15∘−Rsin15∘=100cos60∘−250sin15∘−150sin15∘=−159.59kN(→)=−159.59kN(→)=159.59kN(←)​
Resultant force in y-direction,

Direction with respect to x-axis
=θ+90∘=28.9∘+90∘=118.9∘\begin{aligned} &=\theta+90^{\circ} \\ &=28.9^{\circ}+90^{\circ} \\ &=118.9^{\circ} \end{aligned}​=θ+90∘=28.9∘+90∘=118.9∘​
explanationText: Resultant force in x-direction, $\begin{aligned} R_{x}&=P\cos 60^{\circ}-Q\sin 15^{\circ}-R\sin 15^{\circ} \\ &=100\cos 60^{\circ}-250\sin 15^{\circ}-150\sin 15^{\circ} \\ &=-159.59\, kN\left ( \rightarrow \right ) \\ &=-159.59\, kN\left ( \rightarrow \right ) \\ &=159.59\, kN\left ( \leftarrow \right ) \end{aligned}$ Resultant force in y-direction, $\begin{aligned} R_{y}&=P\sin 60^{\circ}+Q\cos 15^{\circ}-R\sin 15^{\circ} \\ &=100\sin 60^{\circ}+250\cos 15^{\circ}-150\sin 15^{\circ} \\ &=289.26\, kN \left ( \uparrow \right ) \end{aligned}$ Final resultant force, $\begin{aligned} R&=\sqrt{R^{2}_{x}+R^{2}_{y}}=330.4\, kN \\ \theta &=\tan ^{-1}\left ( \frac{159.59}{289.56} \right ) \\ \theta &=28.9^{\circ} \end{aligned}$ Direction with respect to x-axis $\begin{aligned} &=\theta+90^{\circ} \\ &=28.9^{\circ}+90^{\circ} \\ &=118.9^{\circ} \end{aligned}$

questionText: Polar moment of inertia ( $I_{p}$ ), in $cm^{4}$ , of a rectangular section having width, b=2 and depth, d=6 cm is _____
explanationHtml:
Polar moment of inertia,
Ip=Ix+Iy=bd312+db312=bd12(b2+d2)=2×612(22+62)=40  cm4\begin{aligned} I_p&= I_x+I_y\\ &=\frac{bd^3}{12}+\frac{db^3}{12}\\ &=\frac{bd}{12}(b^2+d^2) \\ &= \frac{2 \times 6}{12}(2^2+6^2)\\ &=40\; cm^4 \end{aligned}Ip​​=Ix​+Iy​=12bd3​+12db3​=12bd​(b2+d2)=122×6​(22+62)=40cm4​
explanationText: Polar moment of inertia, $\begin{aligned} I_p&= I_x+I_y\\ &=\frac{bd^3}{12}+\frac{db^3}{12}\\ &=\frac{bd}{12}(b^2+d^2) \\ &= \frac{2 \times 6}{12}(2^2+6^2)\\ &=40\; cm^4 \end{aligned}$

questionMarkup: A disc of radius r has a hole of radius r/2 cut-out as shown. The centroid of the remaining disc (shaded portion) at a radial distance from the centre "O" is
questionText: A disc of radius r has a hole of radius r/2 cut-out as shown. The centroid of the remaining disc (shaded portion) at a radial distance from the centre "O" is
explanationText: The centroid of the shaped portion of the disc is given by, $\; \; \; x=\frac{A_{1}x_{1}+A_{2}x_{2}}{A_{1}+A_{2}}$ where x is the radial distance from O. $\begin{aligned} A_{1}&=\, \pi r^{2};\; x_{1}=0;\\ A_{2}&=-\pi \times \left ( \frac{r}{2} \right )^{2}=-\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\\ x_{2}&=\frac{r}{2}\\ \therefore \; x&=\frac{\pi r^{2}\times 0-\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\times \frac{r}{2}}{\pi r^{2}-\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}}\\ x&=\frac{\pi r^{2}\times 0-\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}\times \frac{r}{2}}{\pi r^{2}-\frac{\pi r^{2}}{4}}\\ \Rightarrow \; x&=-\frac{r}{6} \end{aligned}$
